title: coupon_usage_reservation has no version column: the TTL sweep can revert a COMMITTED redemption to EXPIRED, which un-counts it from the per-user limit and the campaign budget
actual: CouponUsageReservation had no @Version and the table had no version column. ReservationCleanupScheduler.releaseAllExpiredReservations() selected PENDING rows with an unlocked SELECT and then dirty-check-flipped them to EXPIRED (batch.forEach(r -> r.setStatus(UsageStatus.EXPIRED))). A sweep that read the row before commit() ran could therefore overwrite the COMMITTED state. This is the same lost-update class as F-011 in inventory-service. The consequence is money-relevant: CampaignReservationServiceImpl counts PENDING + COMMITTED for both the per-user limit (countByCampaignIdAndUserIdAndStatusIn) and the campaign budget (countByCampaignIdAndStatusIn / sumDiscountByCampaignIdAndStatusIn), so a silently reverted redemption stops being counted - the customer can redeem the same coupon again and the campaign budget is under-spent.
expected: A committed redemption is never reverted, and the limit/budget counters only ever decrease through an explicit release.
trigger: A commit() that runs just before the reservation TTL elapses, racing with the 60-second sweep.
root_cause: No optimistic-locking or conditional-update discipline on the coupon usage reservation aggregate, and the sweep performed a blind read-modify-write.
consequences: Double redemption of the same coupon and campaign budget overspend; no error is raised, the counters simply drift.
remediation: New Liquibase changeset changelog-004 adds coupon_usage_reservation.version; the entity gains @Version; the sweep now CLAIMS each row with a conditional UPDATE (status = PENDING -> EXPIRED, released_at = now, version + 1) so exactly one writer can transition it.
regression_test: promotion-service: ReservationCleanupSchedulerTest.sweep_skipsRowsAlreadyClaimedByAnotherWriter asserts that a claim which affects zero rows leaves the inventory untouched and emits no event.
remediation_applied: changelog-004-coupon-reservation-version.yaml; CouponUsageReservation.@Version; ReservationCleanupScheduler claims rows via reservationRepository.claimForExpiry.

title: The promotion TTL sweep emitted no promotion.released.v1 event, unlike the inventory sweep - the two sweeps had diverged
actual: The promotion sweep's javadoc stated 'NO events to publish - only the status changes' and it indeed wrote no outbox row, while the inventory sweep (after the F-012 remediation) publishes inventory.released.v1 for every swept reservation. The two sweeps therefore had different contracts for the same kind of transition.
expected: Every state transition of a reservation is described by the event stream, or the divergence is deliberate and documented.
trigger: A coupon reservation reaches its TTL and is swept.
root_cause: The two sweeps were written independently against different (inconsistent) contracts.
consequences: shop.promotion.lifecycle.v1 reports a reservation that was never released. The practical impact today is bounded because that topic has no consumer at all (F-002), so the divergence is invisible today but would surface the moment a consumer is added.
remediation: The sweep now publishes promotion.released.v1 (previousStatus=PENDING) in the same transaction as the status transition, matching the inventory sweep and the service-layer release path.
remediation_applied: ReservationCleanupScheduler injects CampaignRepository + PromotionEventPublisher and publishes the released event per claimed reservation.

title: ReservationRetryServiceImpl swallowed the interrupt flag and kept retrying - the same defect as F-014, in a second service
actual: withRetry() caught OptimisticLockingFailureException and called sleep(); sleep() restored the interrupt flag and returned, and the loop continued to the next attempt. Every remaining attempt then failed instantly (the interrupt flag makes Thread.sleep throw immediately) and the caller received a spurious PROMOTION_RESERVATION_VERSION_CONFLICT. This is the identical defect to F-014, which was remediated in inventory-service but not here.
expected: An interrupted request thread aborts the retry loop and propagates the cancellation.
trigger: The client disconnects and the container interrupts the request thread while a version conflict is being retried.
root_cause: The interrupt flag was restored but never acted upon; the loop had no cancellation check.
consequences: A busy retry loop on a dead thread; the caller sees a version-conflict error instead of a cancellation, and the work continues after the client is gone.
remediation: sleep() now returns false when interrupted; the loop restores the flag and aborts with the domain error instead of spinning.
regression_test: promotion-service module suite green; the same shape as the inventory remediation (F-014).
remediation_applied: ReservationRetryServiceImpl.sleep returns a boolean and withRetry aborts on interruption.

title: A concurrent duplicate coupon reserve surfaced a raw DataIntegrityViolationException (HTTP 500) instead of the domain's PROMOTION_DUPLICATE_REQUEST
actual: reserve() looks up an existing reservation by order id and, finding none, inserts a new one. The schema enforces one reservation per order with the UNIQUE index uk_cur_order_id, so a concurrent second reserve for the same order is rejected by the database - but the insert was not wrapped, so the constraint violation escaped as an unhandled DataIntegrityViolationException (HTTP 500) rather than the catalogue's PROMOTION_DUPLICATE_REQUEST.
expected: A duplicate reservation attempt returns the catalogue's conflict code, exactly like the pre-check path does.
trigger: Two concurrent reserve calls for the same order id (a client double-submit, or a saga retry racing the original).
root_cause: The database constraint that makes the check race-free was not mapped to a domain error.
consequences: A 500 instead of a 409 for a normal business conflict; the error also loses the order id context that PROMOTION_DUPLICATE_REQUEST carries.
remediation: Catch DataIntegrityViolationException around the insert and map it to PROMOTION_DUPLICATE_REQUEST with the order id.
regression_test: promotion-service module suite green; the mapping is exercised by the existing duplicate-request test plus the concurrency suite.
remediation_applied: CampaignReservationServiceImpl.reserve maps the unique-constraint violation to ErrorCode.PROMOTION_DUPLICATE_REQUEST.

title: Campaign update silently collapses every non-ACTIVE requested status to INACTIVE
actual: CampaignServiceImpl.update() calls applyStatus(campaign, request.status()), and applyStatus only distinguishes ACTIVE from everything else: a null status deactivates the campaign, and any other CampaignStatus value would also deactivate it rather than being applied.
expected: The requested status is applied, or an unsupported transition is rejected explicitly.
trigger: An operator sends a campaign update without a status field (the field is optional on the request).
root_cause: applyStatus models only the binary active/inactive flag instead of the CampaignStatus enum.
consequences: A PATCH-style update that omits the status silently deactivates a live campaign, which stops every subsequent reserve from succeeding (CAMPAIGN_NOT_ACTIVE) without any explicit signal.
remediation: Only apply the status when the request actually carries one; otherwise leave the current status unchanged.
regression_test: Unit test: an update request without a status must keep the campaign active.

title: CampaignServiceImpl.delete uses the strict orElseThrow() attribution while the rest of the fleet uses orElse("system")
actual: The fleet has two soft-delete attribution conventions. promotion-service and (after the F-037 remediation) tax-service use auditorAware.getCurrentAuditor().orElseThrow(), which throws a raw NoSuchElementException (HTTP 500) when no actor can be resolved. favourite-service and product-service (3 sites) still use orElse("system"), which silently attributes a destructive administrative change to a pseudo-actor and degrades the audit trail.
expected: One convention across the fleet, and a domain error (not a raw NoSuchElementException) when the actor cannot be resolved.
trigger: A destructive soft-delete performed by a caller for which the AuditorAware cannot resolve a principal (a service-to-service call, or an expired security context).
root_cause: Two conventions coexisted; the remediation for F-037 aligned tax-service with promotion-service but did not converge the whole fleet.
consequences: Inconsistent audit attribution for destructive admin operations, and a raw 500 (instead of a clean domain error) where the strict convention is used.
remediation: Add a shared helper in common-core (or common-logging) that requires a resolved actor and raises a BusinessException with an explicit code; use it at every soft-delete site so the fleet has one contract.
regression_test: Unit test per service asserting the delete fails with the domain error when no auditor is resolvable.
